description:
outram-blender can already WRITE OpenFOAM polyMesh three ways (export::to_polymesh_text -> 5 ASCII strings; export::write_polymesh -> disk; feature-gated export::to_poly_mesh -> real outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh). It has NO reader, so a polyMesh cannot be loaded back into a Mesh. Add the import side to complete round-trip polyMesh I/O.

Recommended route (low-risk, no new parser): under the foam bridge feature, add export::from_poly_mesh(&outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh) -> Mesh that converts the PolyMesh points + faceList into the half-edge Mesh boundary surface (Mesh::from_polygons). The foam crate already provides PolyMesh::read(dir) (crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/io/poly_mesh.rs:212), so from_poly_mesh + PolyMesh::read gives full disk read for free. Optionally also a feature-free ASCII parser (points/faces only) for standalone use without the foam dependency.

Caveats to document: a polyMesh is a VOLUME mesh (points/faces/owner/neighbour/cells); outram-blender's Mesh is a boundary surface, so import reconstructs the face soup (all faces), not cells. Winding/owner-neighbour orientation may need a recalc_normals pass.

V&V: round-trip a primitive — write_polymesh(cube) or to_poly_mesh(cube) -> from_poly_mesh -> assert V/E/F/chi == original cube (8/12/6/2), watertight after an optional recalc_normals. Methodology + measured results in the test doc comment per the workspace V&V rule.
title: outram-blender: read polyMesh (import) — round out polyMesh I/O
